title: Verticillium dahliae Pathogenicity and Protein Expression
summary: This cluster revolves around the pathogenic fungus Verticillium dahliae and its interactions with various organisms and proteins. V. dahliae causes disease in cotton and regulates the development of VdMFS2, a gene or protein expressed in cotton. The fungus has multiple proteins, including AAs, CAZymes, CBMs, CEs, G2WZT4, and SCRPs, and is associated with Fradin EF. Vd592, a related organism, has growth mediums and nutrients, and Vd592Y and ΔVdMFS2-4Y have more secreted proteins than their counterparts. The cluster also includes various methods and tools, such as HIGS, pTRV2-00, and Tpk1, and organisms like Agrobacterium tumefaciens and Alternaria alternata.
